data.title: Nipple eczema — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nipple eczema** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What are the causes of nipple/areolar eczema?**
- Atopic dermatitis (minor criterion of Hanifin–Rajka) — commonest, usually bilateral, adolescent girls
- Irritant (friction — 'jogger's nipple', breastfeeding — saliva, pumps), allergic contact (nursing creams, lanolin, fragrances, bra materials), Candida during breastfeeding, scabies (areolae in women), seborrhoeic

**Q2. Why is unilateral persistent nipple eczema a red flag?**
- Paget's disease of the nipple — intra-epidermal spread of underlying ductal breast carcinoma; unilateral, slowly progressive, well-defined, crusted/eroded, may have nipple retraction, discharge, lump
- Any unilateral nipple eczema not responding to 3–4 weeks of topical steroid needs biopsy and breast imaging

**Q3. Differentiate eczema from Paget's disease of nipple.**
- Eczema: bilateral, itchy, ill-defined, starts on areola, fluctuates, responds to steroids, nipple intact
- Paget's: unilateral, little itch, sharply demarcated, starts on nipple then areola, persistent, steroid-unresponsive, nipple may be destroyed/retracted; histology — large pale Paget cells (CK7+, CEA+, HER2+)

**Q4. Other differentials.**
- Psoriasis, erosive adenomatosis of nipple, Bowen's disease, hyperkeratosis of nipple and areola (naevoid), tinea, herpes, scabies

**Q5. Management of nipple eczema in breastfeeding women.**
- Emollient (pure petrolatum), mild topical steroid applied after feeds and wiped before the next feed; treat Candida in mother and baby (oral thrush) with topical azole/nystatin; correct latch; avoid allergenic nursing creams

**Q6. Work-up in a non-healing case.**
- Patch test (if contact allergy), KOH, skin biopsy, mammography/ultrasound for Paget's

**Q7. What is hyperkeratosis of nipple and areola?**
- Rare benign verrucous thickening and pigmentation — naevoid, associated with ichthyosis/AD/ CTCL or oestrogen therapy; keratolytics, retinoids, cryotherapy

**Q8. Describe the histopathology of eczema by stage (PYQ).**
- Acute: marked spongiosis with intraepidermal vesicles, papillary oedema, perivascular lymphocytes ± eosinophils
- Subacute: spongiosis + parakeratosis + acanthosis, crusts
- Chronic: compact hyperkeratosis, irregular/ psoriasiform acanthosis, hypergranulosis, minimal spongiosis, vertical collagen in papillae (lichenification)

**Q9. Classify topical corticosteroids by potency (WHO/ British).**
- Super-potent (class I): clobetasol propionate 0.05%, halobetasol, betamethasone dipropionate in optimised vehicle
- Potent: betamethasone dipropionate/ valerate 0.1%, mometasone furoate 0.1%, fluticasone 0.05%, fluocinolone 0.025%, halcinonide
- Moderate: clobetasone butyrate 0.05%, triamcinolone 0.1%, desonide, hydrocortisone butyrate
- Mild: hydrocortisone 1–2.5%
- Ointments more potent than creams of same molecule; avoid potent on face, flexures, genitals, infants

**Q10. Breastfeeding nipple pain — differentials.**
- Poor latch/ trauma (fissures), candidiasis (burning, shooting pain, shiny pink nipple — treat mother and baby), bacterial infection (S. aureus — fissures with crusts), vasospasm/ Raynaud's of nipple (blanching, pain after feeds — nifedipine), contact dermatitis (creams, pump parts), eczema, herpes

**Q11. Nipple involvement in atopic dermatitis — features.**
- Bilateral scaly, fissured, itchy erythema of areola and nipple in adolescent girls/ young women; part of Hanifin–Rajka minor criteria; responds to mild steroids/ tacrolimus and emollients

**Q12. Imaging and biopsy in suspected Paget's disease.**
- Mammography + ultrasound ± MRI breast to find underlying carcinoma (present in >90%); punch/ wedge biopsy of nipple skin; refer to breast surgeon — mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy

**Q13. What is the histopathology of Paget's disease of the nipple?**
- Large round pale cells with abundant clear/amphophilic cytoplasm and large nuclei scattered singly and in nests throughout the epidermis (pagetoid spread), sparing the basal layer partially; CK7+, CEA+, EMA+, HER2 often +, CK20− (unlike secondary extramammary Paget's)

**Q14. Differentiate mammary from extramammary Paget's disease.**
- Mammary: nipple/areola, almost always underlying ductal carcinoma
- Extramammary: apocrine-rich skin (vulva, perianal, scrotum, axilla) — primary intraepidermal adenocarcinoma (CK7+, GCDFP-15+) or secondary to underlying colorectal (CK20+) or urothelial (uroplakin+) cancer; 'strawberries and cream' red plaques with white scale; treat with Mohs/excision, imiquimod, PDT

## Quick spotter facts
- Unilateral, steroid-resistant nipple 'eczema' — biopsy for Paget's disease

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Eczemas, breast dermatoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
